minutes.headline: Committee approved posting two grant-funded positions, suspended school choice, and named a COVID MOA negotiator.
minutes.summary: The committee approved posting a long-term nurse sub and a part-time school psychologist, both funded by grants rather than local money. A MASC presenter then led a workshop on superintendent evaluation.

budget_items.topic: Two grant-funded positions not in local budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Two positions were requested for posting; neither is in the local budget and both are funded by DESE grants, with insurance paid from the grants.
Salary is split between the COVID school reopening grant (September to December) and the elementary and secondary schools emergency relief fund (January to June).
Estimated cost matches the amount in the spring preliminary budgets and is fully funded by both grants.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to let the business manager post two grant-funded positions, a long-term nurse substitute and a part-time school psychologist.
The committee voted to temporarily suspend the school choice program.
The committee voted to nominate Carol as its representative for COVID MOA bargaining.
The 2020-2021 school calendar revision was tabled until the next week's meeting so the superintendent can talk with union leadership.
A MASC presenter led a workshop on superintendent evaluation and is to return on August 19th.

why_it_matters: The two new positions are paid from DESE grants rather than the local budget, so they add school staff without adding to the tax levy in the year they are funded.
Suspending school choice and the unsettled 2020-2021 calendar affect which students enroll and when school days fall, and the COVID MOA bargaining will set working terms for reopening.
watch_next: The tabled 2020-2021 school calendar revision is due back at next week's meeting.
The MASC presenter returns August 19th, and subcommittee updates (TC Passios and athletic advisory) go on the next agenda.
